likely_bottleneck: High-aspect-ratio plasma profile control with low damage
why_likely: Public technical material repeatedly couples anisotropy, selectivity, profile, residue, particles, and damage; advanced memory pushes aspect ratio higher.
observable_signals: HAR language in annual reports; ICP/CCP product emphasis; etch process and RF job postings.
caveats: Public pages show target performance and applications more clearly than real yield-learning depth.
suggested_primary_sources: AMEC annual reports and etch pages; CNIPA; CNKI; recruiting pages

likely_bottleneck: Post-etch clean and strip that remove residues without pattern loss
why_likely: Patterned cleaning and strip require simultaneous residue removal, particle control, and no-damage behavior, especially after aggressive etch.
observable_signals: Megasonic/no-damage cleaning pages; strip-tool disclosures; clean-process job titles.
caveats: Customer-specific chemistries and rework heuristics are often private.
suggested_primary_sources: ACM Research Shanghai product pages; CNIPA; CNKI; application-engineer postings

likely_bottleneck: Conformal HAR film growth at production-worthy throughput
why_likely: Official sources openly recognize the tradeoff between ALD-like conformality and throughput, and the need for batch/vertical solutions.
observable_signals: ALD/LPCVD product mix; validation and repeat-order disclosures; film-process job ads.
caveats: Repeat orders are a helpful signal but do not reveal full chamber-match difficulty.
suggested_primary_sources: NAURA ALD/LPCVD pages and article; AMEC annual reports; CNINFO

likely_bottleneck: Coupling precursor chemistry to stable chamber behavior and low particles
why_likely: Lab film quality is easier than stable HVM performance across PM cycles and chamber populations.
observable_signals: In-situ clean messaging; chamber-match language; maintenance and application roles; patents on gas delivery and chamber materials.
caveats: Public filings may under-describe maintenance sensitivity and excursion modes.
suggested_primary_sources: NAURA and AMEC product pages and annual reports; CNIPA; company ATS

likely_bottleneck: Optics-plus-algorithms integration that reduces false alarms without losing sensitivity
why_likely: Inspection and metrology tools publicly emphasize illumination, classification, AI/ML, and yield-ramp support, implying a hard hardware-software boundary problem.
observable_signals: Optical-design and algorithm hiring; product language on ADC, AI, classification, and yield excursion control.
caveats: Private datasets and customer libraries mean papers and patents undercount operational skill.
suggested_primary_sources: KLA official pages; Skyverse and SMEE product pages; recruitment pages

why_likely: Measurement trust in production depends on calibration, matching, nuisance suppression, and tool-to-tool consistency at customer sites.
observable_signals: Field support roles; annual reports on support teams; service-page language; training plans.
caveats: The best know-how is often buried in service routines rather than formal R&D outputs.
suggested_primary_sources: Skyverse annual reports and ATS; SMEE service pages; CNINFO

likely_bottleneck: Opto-mechatronic integration for overlay, focus, and stability
why_likely: ASML’s public decomposition of lithography and SMEE’s published skill requirements both point to a rare combination of optics, mechanics, control, and calibration.
observable_signals: Optical-design job requirements; lithography product pages stressing focus/overlay/backside alignment.
caveats: This row is a sidebar inference for atlas design, not a claim about exact labor shortage magnitude.
suggested_primary_sources: ASML lithography pages; SMEE product and recruitment pages; CNIPA

likely_bottleneck: Service calibration, contamination discipline, and process-window recovery
why_likely: Lithography performance degrades when optics-path cleanliness, calibration, or process window drifts; service and recovery routines are highly experience-based.
observable_signals: Service pages; training academy pages; field-service hiring; support network disclosures.
caveats: Public pages expose training structures more than the true content of recovery know-how.
suggested_primary_sources: ASML lithography pages; SMEE service and training pages; official recruitment pages
